study_families.study_label: UCI PERC adolescent endurance-training monocyte transcriptome study
study_families.design: Single-cohort, within-subject repeated-measures design: acute intermittent cycling exercise challenge administered on a separate laboratory visit before and after an 8-wk supervised endurance (+ brief strength) training intervention; paired pre/post-acute-exercise blood sampling at each of the two visits; no non-exercising control group (explicit limitation).
study_families.registry_ids: NR (no clinical-trial registry number stated in text; IRB approval only)
study_families.training_load: 8-wk program, 3 sessions/wk: 40-50 min aerobic endurance exercise (cycle ergometer, treadmill walk/jog, elliptical, rowing) at 65-75% age-predicted HRmax, progressive intensity, plus 5-8 min supplementary muscle-strengthening work/session (M2 multi-gym/mat exercises); frequency/duration held constant after a 2-wk adaptation period.
study_families.cointerventions: Brief supplementary strength work bundled with the endurance training intervention (not separable from the endurance component in the reported design).
study_families.study_notes: IRB: University of California, Irvine; written informed assent (child) and parental/guardian consent obtained. Funded by NIH U01 TR002004 (REACH project) plus institutional core-facility grants. No conflicts of interest declared. Elite athletes, vigorous competitive-sport participants, and volunteers with chronic medical conditions or medication use were excluded at recruitment.

reports.title: Endurance training attenuates acute exercise-induced monocyte transcriptomic responses in adolescents: sex-specific molecular adaptations
reports.authors: Plaza-Florido A; Haddad F; Cooper DM; Radom-Aizik S
reports.version_date: First published online 2026-08-03; print J Appl Physiol 141:873-887, 2026; Submitted 2026-03-24, Revised 2026-07-06, Accepted 2026-07-27
reports.version_label: NR (single version of record identified; no correction/erratum found)
source_locator: p.873 header/citation block and running head
reports.reviewer_notes: provisional FT code: FT03. All 21 participants are adolescents 13-17 y (p.873 Abstract: 'Twelve males and nine females (13-17 yr)'; p.876 Table 1: age 15.2+-1.3 y males, 15.2+-1.5 y females); no adult (>=18 y) participants and no separable adult stratum exist in this report, so under contract 2.3 / fulltext_exclusion_codes.json FT03 ('Population outside target (under 18 y...)') this is excluded from the peer-reviewed core A/B map. cohorts.adult_stratum_separable is recorded as 'all_participants_under_18' (a fully-pediatric cohort), not 'mixed_age...not_separable' as the pilot_purpose free-text summary states -- see unresolved_questions for this wording discrepancy between pilot_manifest.json/PILOT_README.md and the controlled-vocabulary value that actually fits this report. Otherwise this report would plausibly satisfy A_core_acute (identifiable single bout, pre-exercise baseline, immediate post-exercise sample, direct monocyte count + monocyte transcriptome) and would additionally qualify for a training-adaptation comparison (acute challenge repeated before/after an 8-wk intervention), but population ineligibility is dispositive and is evaluated before exposure/sampling criteria per the FT01-FT08 hierarchy.
reports.author_stated_use: Authors explicitly frame findings as mechanistic/hypothesis-generating only, not as validated biomarkers: 'the identified pathways should primarily be interpreted as mechanistic and hypothesis-generating insights into exercise-induced immune regulation during adolescence, rather than direct biomarkers of clinical benefit' (p.883); stated long-range motivation is early-life cardiovascular-disease prevention research, not any monitoring/diagnostic/return-to-training application.
author_window_interpretation_locator: Full-text search found no instance of 'open window', 'immunosuppression', 'susceptibility' or 'redistribution' anywhere in the article (Abstract through References, p.873-887); the paper's framing is cardiovascular-disease risk / trained-innate-immunity, not infection-risk open-window susceptibility (p.883-884 Discussion: 'consistent with emerging concepts of exercise-induced immune adaptation and trained innate immunity').

measurements.multiplicity: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction across all quantified transcripts per paired comparison (RNA-seq rows); Bonferroni post hoc for ANOVA-based physiological covariates.
measurements.confounding: NR (no covariate adjustment beyond sex-stratified analysis and baseline-value ANCOVA covariates for VO2peak/body weight; not applicable to this measurement)

eligibility_opinion.rationale: All 21 participants are adolescents aged 13-17 y with no adults enrolled (p.873 Abstract: 'Twelve males and nine females (13-17 yr)'; p.876 Table 1: age 15.2+-1.3 y males / 15.2+-1.5 y females), so there is no adult (>=18 y) stratum to separate out, and under v3 contract 2.3 / fulltext_exclusion_codes.json this establishes FT03 (population not eligible) ahead of any exposure/sampling/immune-link assessment in the FT01-FT08 hierarchy. Had the population criterion been met, the identifiable acute cycling bout with a pre-exercise baseline, an immediate post-exercise sample, and direct monocyte count plus monocyte transcriptome measurements would otherwise plausibly have supported A_core_acute, with a secondary training-adaptation comparison (same participants, acute challenge repeated before/after an 8-wk endurance intervention).

unresolved_questions: Wording mismatch, pilot_purpose vs controlled vocabulary: pilot_manifest.json/PILOT_README.md describe R62 as a case where the adult stratum is 'not separable' ('不可分出成人层'), but the cohort is in fact 100% adolescent (13-17 y) with zero adults -- the controlled-vocabulary value that actually fits is cohorts.adult_stratum_separable = 'all_participants_under_18', not 'mixed_age_adult_stratum_not_separable'. Both values map to FT03, so the screening outcome is unaffected, but this is itself a useful calibration finding: should the pilot_purpose free text and the controlled vocabulary be reconciled (e.g. is there a genuinely mixed-age FT03 example elsewhere in the full corpus, or was 'adolescent cohort' always meant to exercise the all-under-18 branch of the same code)?

Exact timepoint of the one missing before-training male monocyte-count data point (Fig. 2 legend states n=11 'before the training period' without specifying baseline vs immediate-post vs both) could not be resolved from the main text; recorded as UNCLEAR with low confidence in sample_sets SS-R62-09/SS-R62-10 rather than guessed.

Whether the one female participant missing the after-training immediate-post blood sample (p.875, p.877) also had a usable after-training baseline sample that was simply excluded from the paired DE analysis, or never had a baseline sample drawn at all, is not fully disambiguated in the main text; both after-training female RNA-seq rows (SS-R62-07/SS-R62-08) are recorded at n=8 per Fig. 3's reported analytic n, with this caveat flagged at medium/low confidence.

Row-unit calibration question for this report design: sample_sets were split by sex x training-phase x timepoint x matrix (24 rows total) because n genuinely differs by sex at several timepoints and the paper's own primary analysis axis is sex-by-time interaction; an alternative, coarser convention (collapsing sex into age_sex_stratum within fewer rows, accepting a single reported range for n_participants) would produce far fewer rows. Which convention the full review should standardize on for sex-stratified designs is a concrete item for the manual.

Measurement-table completeness for excluded/FT03 boundary reports: only 10 representative measurement rows (1 assay-universe summary + 8 named transcript/ncRNA candidates drawn from Table 2/Table 4/Discussion + monocyte count + lactate) were extracted here, following the same non-exhaustive precedent already set for R61 in this same pilot batch, rather than itemizing every gene in Supplemental Tables S2, S4, S5, S7 and S8 (which were also not locally accessible). Confirm with D/A whether FT03 boundary-case reports should receive this lighter representative pass, or the full candidate universe, for the formal manual.

Supplemental Tables S1-S8 and Fig. S1 (figshare DOI 10.6084/m9.figshare.31724731) were not included in the institutionally-fetched PDF (per fulltexts_manifest.json) and were not fetched for this task (no web requests permitted); several supplement_availability values are therefore 'linked_but_not_accessible' rather than 'accessible' or 'not_checked', and some named-candidate numeric values (e.g. HDAC9, THBD, SCAMP1-AS1 exact log2FC) could not be located and are recorded as NR/'named_candidate_result_not_located'.

No trial-registry number is reported anywhere in the text (only IRB approval); study_families.registry_ids is recorded as NR rather than NA, since it is plausible (though unconfirmed) that this type of mechanistic pediatric exercise study was never prospectively registered -- confirm whether NR or NA is the more appropriate code for 'registry not required/not used' versus 'registry status simply not reported'.
